messages.content: Now I need to settle the Seattle hotel for June 14 through 17. Please compare staying in one place with splitting the stay, and account for both the daytime meetings and Tuesday evening author event.

I found three workable arrangements. The Hyatt Regency, where the daytime meetings are being held, has rooms only Sunday and Monday nights at $259 per night. The Westin has all three nights at $276 per night and is about a nine-minute walk from the Hyatt. The Silver Cloud on Broadway also has all three nights at $248 per night; it is closest to Tuesday's author event but would require a longer trip to the Hyatt each meeting day.
What are the actual totals with tax, and where exactly is the Tuesday event?

The author event is at Elliott Bay Book Company at 7:00 p.m. Tuesday, June 16. Using the quoted 15.7% lodging tax, the Hyatt is $599.33 for its two available nights, the Westin is $958.00 for all three nights, and the Silver Cloud is $860.81 for all three. No mandatory property fee was shown on these rates, but that needs confirmation on the final booking screen.
If I split, I would do the Hyatt Sunday and Monday, then move near the bookstore Tuesday. How does that compare?

Two Hyatt nights plus Tuesday night at the Silver Cloud would total about $886.27. That saves approximately $71.73 versus three nights at the Westin, but you would need to check out Tuesday morning, store or move your luggage, and then travel back toward the Hyatt for Tuesday's meetings. On Wednesday, the Silver Cloud is roughly 1.3 miles from the Hyatt, so reaching the final meeting and retrieving luggage before the planned 5:15 p.m. airport departure would require extra coordination.
How inconvenient is the Westin for the bookstore Tuesday night?

The Westin is approximately 1.2 miles from Elliott Bay Book Company. A car would generally take about 8 to 12 minutes outside a traffic spike; public transit or walking would take longer. From the Hyatt after Tuesday's meetings, you could walk back to the Westin, leave work materials in the room, and take a short ride to the event without changing hotels.
That sounds cleaner. Before deciding, give me the cancellation terms for all three rates.

The Hyatt rate can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. Seattle time on Thursday, June 11. The Westin rate is refundable until 11:59 p.m. Seattle time on Friday, June 12. The Silver Cloud rate requires cancellation at least 48 hours before its 3:00 p.m. arrival time, making the cutoff 3:00 p.m. Sunday, June 14 for a Tuesday-only stay, or Friday, June 12 for a Sunday arrival. After the applicable deadline, each property lists a one-night room-and-tax penalty.
So the split saves only about $72 and gives me two moves during the workday, counting the luggage retrieval Wednesday.

Correct. The split is cheaper, but it introduces a Tuesday checkout and transfer plus a Wednesday luggage stop before the airport. The Westin costs more but keeps you within walking distance of the daytime site and avoids changing rooms during the trip.
Select the Westin for all three nights. Prepare the reservation details, but don't book it yet because I want the live total checked together with the flight.

The prepared hotel request is for one adult at the Westin Seattle, checking in Sunday, June 14 and checking out Wednesday, June 17, for three nights. The current quote is $276 per night, or $958.00 including the displayed tax, with cancellation allowed through 11:59 p.m. Seattle time on June 12. No reservation has been submitted.
Use a king room if the quoted rate includes one, but don't pay extra or switch rates for it. What remains to verify?

The Westin is now the selected, unbooked hotel. Before authorization, I will verify that the $276 refundable rate and $958.00 total are still available, confirm whether a king room is included at that price, check for any destination or facility fee, confirm the cancellation deadline and one-night penalty, and review the final deposit terms. The selected United flights also still need their live fare, schedule, baggage terms, and restrictions rechecked. Nothing has been purchased or reserved.
